The '''2020 [[Eliteserien]]''' was the 76th <!-- completed -->season of top-tier [[Association football|football]] in Norway. This was fourth season of Eliteserien as rebranding from Tippeligaen. 

The season was scheduled to begin on 4 April. However, due to the [[COVID-19 pandemic in Norway]] the opening games of the season were delayed. It was first delayed until 2 May,<ref name="nrk">{{cite news |url=https://www.nrk.no/sport/store-endringar-i-fotballen_-meisterligaen-og-eliteserien-blir-utsett-1.14941079 |title=Store endringar i fotballen: Eliteserien blir stoppa |language=no |work=[[NRK]] |date=12 March 2020 |access-date=12 March 2020}}</ref> then further delayed until 23 May.<ref name="second delay">{{cite web |url=https://www.fotball.no/tema/nff-nyheter/2020/seriestarten-for-kvinner-og-menn-skyves-til-slutten-av-mai/ |title=Seriestarten for kvinner og menn flyttes til slutten av mai |language=no |website=[[Norwegian Football Federation]] |date=24 March 2020 |access-date=24 March 2020}}</ref> The season was scheduled to end 29 November 2020, not including play-off matches, but was rescheduled to conclude on 22 December.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.fotball.no/turneringer/eliteserien/2019/endring-i-hovedterminlisten/ |title=Eliteserien 2020 |language=no |website=[[Norwegian Football Federation]] |date=7 October 2019}}</ref> On 7 May, the Norwegian government allowed the league to start on 16 June with full training starting immediately.<ref>{{cite news |url=https://www.tv2.no/sport/11432823/ |title=Helland om gladnyhet: – Jeg gleder meg til å bli sparket ned |work=[[TV 2 (Norway)|TV 2]] |date=7 May 2020 |access-date=19 May 2020}}</ref>

[[Molde FK|Molde]] were the defending champions. [[Aalesunds FK|Aalesund]], [[Sandefjord Fotball|Sandefjord]] and [[IK Start|Start]] joined as the promoted clubs from the [[2019 1. divisjon]]. They replaced [[Lillestrøm SK|Lillestrøm]], [[Tromsø IL|Tromsø]] and [[Ranheim Fotball|Ranheim]] who were relegated to the [[2020 1. divisjon]].

==Effects of the COVID-19 pandemic==
The season was scheduled to begin on 4 April, but on 12 March it was revealed that the first five rounds of the season were postponed and the opening game therefore would be delayed until 2 May due to the [[COVID-19 pandemic in Norway]].<ref>{{cite news |url=https://www.vg.no/sport/fotball/i/kJOyPX/seriestarten-er-utsatt-til-mai |title=Seriestarten er utsatt til mai |language=no |newspaper=[[Verdens Gang]] |date=12 March 2020 |access-date=16 March 2020}}</ref><ref name="nrk"/> On 24 March, the [[Norwegian Football Federation]] announced that the football season was further delayed till 23 May.<ref name="second delay"/> On 7 May, the Norwegian government allowed the teams to begin with full training starting immediately, and opened for the league season to start on 16 June. On 12 June, the NFF announced that 200 spectators would be allowed to attend the games.<ref>{{cite news |url=https://www.vg.no/sport/fotball/i/b5E4X3/nff-aapner-for-200-tilskuere-paa-eliteseriekamper |title=NFF åpner for 200 tilskuere på eliteseriekamper |language=no |newspaper=[[Verdens Gang]] |date=12 June 2020 |access-date=22 June 2020}}</ref>
On 30 September, the [[Minister of Culture and Church Affairs]], [[Abid Raja]], announced that clubs would be able to have crowds of 600 at games from 12 October.<ref>{{cite news |title=RBK-TOPP MISFORNØYD MED 600 TILSKUERE – MENER 6000 HADDE VÆRT UPROBLEMATISK |url=https://www.vg.no/sport/fotball/i/41d2Rg/rbk-topp-misfornoeyd-med-600-tilskuere-mener-6000-hadde-vaert-uproblematisk |newspaper=Verdens Gang |access-date=18 October 2020 |language=no |date=30 September 2020}}</ref>

==Teams==
Sixteen teams compete in the league – the top thirteen teams from the previous season, and three teams promoted from [[2019 1. divisjon|1. division]]. The promoted teams were [[Aalesunds FK|Aalesund]] (after an absence of two years), [[Sandefjord Fotball|Sandefjord]] and [[IK Start|Start]] (both returning to the top flight after one season's absence). They replaced [[Lillestrøm SK|Lillestrøm]], [[Tromsø IL|Tromsø]] and [[Ranheim Fotball|Ranheim]], ending their top flight spells of forty-five, five and two years respectively.

Due to [[COVID-19 pandemic|COVID-19]] restrictions only 200 people were allowed in each match at the beginning of the season.<ref name=NFF>{{cite news|title=NFF åpner for 200 tilskuere på Eliteseriekamper|trans-title=NFF allows 200 spectators at the Eliteserien matches|last=Gjerde|first=Yngve|display-authors=etal|url=https://www.vg.no/sport/fotball/i/b5E4X3/nff-aapner-for-200-tilskuere-paa-eliteseriekamper |newspaper=Verdens Gang|language=no|date=12 June 2020|access-date=17 April 2021}}</ref><ref name=NFF2>{{cite news|title=Fra 12. oktober åpnes det for 600 tilskuere på fotballkamp|trans-title=From 12 October, 600 spectators will be allowed at football matches|last=Stanisic Waagaard|first=Mari|url=https://www.fotball.no/tema/nff-nyheter/2020/apner-for-600-tilskuere-pa-fotballkamper/ |website=[[Norwegian Football Federation|NFF]]|language=no|date=30 September 2020|access-date=17 April 2021}}</ref>

Two clubs were punished for [[Racism in association football|incidents of racism during their matches]], having to play certain games without attendants.<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.fotball.no/lov-og-reglement/beslutninger-fra-utvalg/2020/sandefjord-dommes-til-tomme-tribuner-og-bot/|title=Sandefjord dømmes til tomme tribuner og bot|website=[[Norwegian Football Federation]]|first=Christer|last=Madsen|date=3 December 2020|access-date=17 April 2021|language=no}}</ref><ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.vg.no/sport/i/0KKPoE/sandefjord-vakt-og-aalesund-straffet-for-rasisme-bot-og-tomme-tribuner|title=Sandefjord-vakt og Aalesund straffet for rasisme - bot og tomme tribuner|work=[[Verdens Gang]]|first1=Ida|last1=Høidalen|first2=Oda|last2=Ording|date=11 November 2020|access-date=17 April 2021|language=no}}</ref>
